content.text: No exclusivity obligation binds the Customer anywhere in the agreement.

input.quote: 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: The agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Customer. Section 12.3 expressly confirms Customer may engage any supplier and has made no exclusivity, non-compete, or minimum-volume commitment, and Section 2.1 states there is no minimum quantity or purchase commitment and that declining further Order Forms is not a breach. The only exclusivity-type restraint (12.4, barring Vendor from marketing a directly competing analytics service) runs against Vendor and benefits Customer, which the rule treats as acceptable. Other "exclusive" hits are unrelated (non-exclusive licence in 13, exclusive remedy/jurisdiction language). Preferred position met; no redline needed.
